questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some J are T.

II. No T is V.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some V are J.

II. All J are T.

options.text: Both conclusion I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff8a4c0afaafc16451e4bf2ad3b7f315e82dd30a6535f263598e6fe1f76905f6.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some V are J → False (There are no direct relation given. Hence, false)

II. All J are T → False (it is possible not definite)

Thus, Neither conclusion follow.

questions.question:
By interchanging which two signs the equation will be correct?

13 – 9 × 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3
questions.solution:
Given equation:- 13 – 9 × 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3

After interchanging two signs according to the options,

1) – and ÷

13 ÷ 9 × 2 - 3 + 16 = 3

1.45 × 2 – 3 + 16 = 3

2.90 – 3 + 16 = 3

18.90 – 3 = 3

15.90 = 3 False

2) – and ×

13 × 9 – 2 ÷ 3 + 16 = 3

117 – 0.67 + 16 = 3

133 – 0.67 = 3

132.33 = 3 False

**3) – and +**

**13 + 9 × 2 ÷ 3 - 16 = 3**

**13 + 6 – 16 = 3**

**19 – 16 = 3**

**3 = 3 True**

So, option 3 is true then no need to check the remaining option.

Thus, the correct answer is “- and +”.

questions.question:
Five subjects S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5 (not necessarily in the same order) are to be taught from Monday to Friday. One subject will be taught on one day. Only S5 is taught before S1. S2 is taught before S4. S2 will not be taught on Wednesday.

Which of the following pair of subjects is taught after S3?
questions.solution:
1) Only S5 is taught before S1. (Means S1 taught on Tuesday and S5 is taught on Monday because of this statement).

2) S2 is taught before S4 and S2 will not taught on Wednesday. (Means S2 is taught on Thursday).

3) S3 was taught on the remaining days i.e Wednesday.

questions.question: Six tailors T₁, T₂, T₃, T₄, T₅ and T₆ are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (Not necessarily in the same order). T₂ is second to the right of T₁. T₅ is to the immediate right of T₃. T₃ and T₄ are facing towards each other. Three of the four given options follows a same logic. Which of the following does not follow that logic?
questions.solution:
1) T₃ and T₄ are facing towards each other.

2) T₅ is to the immediate right of T₃.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ed4a25660ac3b90e2f394237d604d2a44ae914f0c9a792c91355f31bbb455e0.png] 

3) T₂ is second to the right of T₁.

4) T₆ is sitting at the remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6d5709f6f599a21a9cc2ca11e8990edd15876d0b233fa787d4efbdfbcee17e1.png] 

Option (1): T₂, T₃ → T₂ is sitting 2ⁿd left of T₃.

Option (2): T4, T6 → T4 is sitting 2nd left of T₆.

Option (3): T6, T5 → T₆ is sitting 2nd left of T₅.

Option (4): T1, T3 → T₁ is sitting 2nd **right **of T₃.

As Option (4) does not follow same logic like other three options.

Thus, the correct answer is **“T₁, T₃”.**

questions.question:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

14, 17, 22, 29, 40, ?
In a certain code language, ‘COW’ is written as ‘41’, ‘PIG’ is written as ‘32’. What is the code for ‘CUP’ in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:-

Sum of the place value of the given words.

COW → C + O + W = 3 + 15 + 23 = 41;

PIG → P + I + G = 16 + 9 + 7 = 32;

Similarly,

**CUP → C + U + P = 3 + 21 + 16 = 40.**

Thus, the correct answer is “40”.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All K are B.

II. No T is K.

**Conclusions:**

I. No K is T.

II. Some B are K.

III. Some T are B.

options.text: Both conclusion II and III follows
Both conclusion I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17f357fe449166f054c8d92725264ad43ac5468520d96c3e81b39a2bc7bc8ea9.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. No K is T → True (No T is K so No K is T are true) 

II. Some B are K → True (All K are B so Some B are K is true)

III. Some T are B → False (There are no direct relation given. Hence, false)

Thus, Both conclusion I and II follows.
